example_1: Don’t worry—we’ll figure it out.
example_2: I need to figure out how to fix the software error.

situation: 즉시 답하기 어렵거나 잠깐 멈추고 싶을 때
example_1: Hang on a second—I’ll check the details.
example_2: Hang on, I’m not ready yet.

situation: 상대에게 중요한 점을 상기시킬 때
example_1: Keep in mind that the deadline is next Friday.
example_2: Keep in mind that parking can be difficult downtown.

situation: 가치가 크지 않을 수 있는 의견이나 정보라도 덧붙일 때
example_1: For what it’s worth, I think the first version was better.
example_2: For what it’s worth, you might want to double-check the address.

situation: 상대 말이나 상황이 논리적으로 납득될 때
example_1: Your explanation makes sense now.
example_2: I’m not sure this plan makes sense for our schedule.

situation: 사정을 종합해 판단을 내릴 때
nuance: 상황을 균형 있게 바라보는 성숙한 톤
example_1: All things considered, it was a good decision.
example_2: All things considered, we managed to finish on time.

situation: 결론을 내리거나 상황과 무관하게 진행할 때
example_1: In any case, we’ll handle it from here.
example_2: I can’t stay long, but in any case, thanks for the help.

situation: 원치 않는 상황을 말하며 상대를 배려할 때
example_1: The last thing I want is for you to feel pressured.
example_2: The last thing I want is to miss the deadline.

situation: 능력이나 가능성을 말할 때
nuance: 일상에서 자연스럽게 쓰는 가능 표현(예: can/might)
example_1: I’m not sure I’ll be able to make it tomorrow.
example_2: Once you get used to it, you’ll be able to do it quickly.

situation: 남은 시간이 부족해질 때
example_1: We’re running out of time, so let’s wrap up.
example_2: I ran out of time to finish the form.

situation: 표현을 바꿔 더 쉽게/명확히 말할 때
example_1: To put it another way, we need a simpler workflow.
example_2: To put it another way, it’s not about effort—it’s about focus.

situation: 감기/컨디션 저하 등 가벼운 병 때문에 컨디션이 나쁠 때
example_1: I can’t come in today—I’m feeling under the weather.
example_2: He skipped work because he was under the weather.

situation: 무언가 잘 풀리길 바라며 기대할 때
example_1: I’ve got an interview tomorrow—keep your fingers crossed for me.
example_2: We submitted the application. Let’s keep our fingers crossed.

situation: 둘 다 같은 목표나 이해를 공유할 때
example_1: Before we start, let’s make sure we’re on the same page.
example_2: I think we’re on the same page about the timeline.

situation: 진행 상황을 계속 듣고 있는지 확인/요청할 때
example_1: Can you keep me in the loop about any changes?
example_2: I wasn’t in the loop, so I missed the meeting.

situation: 자신의 의견이나 사실을 솔직하게 털어놓고 싶을 때
nuance: 조심스럽게 진정성을 전하는 느낌(직설이지만 공격적이지 않음)
example_1: To be honest with you, I was surprised by the result.
example_2: To be honest with you, I’m not sure we have enough time.

expression: it depends on what you mean
situation: 상대의 말이 모호할 때 의미를 확인하며 조율할 때
example_1: It depends on what you mean by “quick”—do you mean 10 minutes or 30?
example_2: It depends on what you mean by “better.” Better for whom?

expression: the thing is, I’m not ready yet
translation_ko: 문제는, 아직 준비가 안 됐다는 거예요
situation: 상대 요청을 바로 거절하기보다 이유를 깔끔히 설명할 때
example_1: The thing is, I’m not ready yet, so can we push it to tomorrow?
example_2: The thing is, I don’t want to rush the decision.

expression: on the one hand... on the other hand...
situation: 장단점을 비교하며 균형 있게 말할 때
example_1: On the one hand, it’s cheaper; on the other hand, it takes longer.
example_2: On the one hand, I enjoy working from home; on the other hand, I miss seeing people.

situation: 상대의 주장에 부드럽게 반박할 때
example_1: I wouldn’t say that’s true—there are definitely some exceptions.
example_2: I wouldn’t say that’s true, but I understand why you think that.

expression: let me think for a second
situation: 답을 바로 못 하겠거나 잠깐 판단이 필요할 때
example_1: Let me think for a second—where did I put the keys?
example_2: Let me think for a second, and I’ll get back to you.

situation: 상대의 논리/설명을 납득했을 때 동의하며 반응할 때
example_1: You don’t want to rush it—that makes sense.
example_2: I see what you mean. That makes sense.

situation: 상대와 생각/이해를 맞출 때
example_1: Don’t worry—I’m on the same page as you.
example_2: If I understand you correctly, we’re on the same page.

situation: 말을 정정하거나 의도를 분명히 할 때
example_1: To be clear, I’m not blaming you. I’m just saying we need a better plan.
example_2: To be clear, I mean this week, not next week.

expression: at the end of the day
situation: 복잡한 상황을 요약하며 최종 결론을 말할 때
nuance: 현실적인 결론/체념에 가까운 톤(맥락에 따라 중립~단호)
example_1: At the end of the day, it’s about choosing what you can live with.
example_2: At the end of the day, we all want the same outcome.

situation: 원하지 않는 행동/상황을 정중히 거절할 때
example_1: I’d rather not discuss it in front of everyone.
example_2: I’d rather not take the risk without more information.

expression: thanks for getting back to me
situation: 이메일/메시지에 답을 받았을 때
example_1: Thanks for getting back to me so quickly.
example_2: Thanks for getting back to me—I appreciate it.

situation: 도움이나 배려에 감사를 표현할 때
example_1: I appreciate it. That really helps.
example_2: I appreciate you taking the time to explain.

situation: 매우 솔직한 의견이나 평가를 강조해서 말할 때
nuance: 강한 직설이지만 여전히 무례하지 않게 포장하는 톤
example_1: To be perfectly honest, I wasn’t impressed with the presentation.
example_2: To be perfectly honest, I think we can do better than this.

situation: 설명이 이해되지 않거나 논리가 헷갈릴 때
example_1: I’m not sure I follow. Can you explain it another way?
example_2: I’m not sure I follow what you mean by “scope.”

situation: 오해를 바로잡을 때
example_1: Sorry— that’s not what I meant. I meant we should be more careful.
example_2: I think there’s a misunderstanding. That’s not what I meant.

translation_ko: 맞는 말이 있어요 / 그건 포인트가 있네요
situation: 상대의 주장에 일부 동의할 때
example_1: You’ve got a point. Maybe we should review the numbers again.
example_2: I see your argument. You’ve got a point about the timing.

situation: 자신의 의도를 설명하려고 말을 고칠 때
nuance: 표현을 다듬는 노력의 톤(대화 흐름 유지)
example_1: I’m trying to say that this isn’t just a quick fix—it’s a long-term issue.
example_2: I’m trying to say that I’m supportive, but I have concerns.

situation: 당장 다음 행동 전까지 임시로 할 일을 말할 때
example_1: In the meantime, you can review the notes I sent you.
example_2: The repairs will take a few hours. In the meantime, we can grab coffee.

expression: to be honest, I had doubts
situation: 초기에 망설였던 점이나 우려를 고백할 때
example_1: To be honest, I had doubts at first, but it turned out fine.
example_2: To be honest, I had doubts about the plan, but now I get it.

situation: 미팅/약속을 잡고 싶다고 정중히 말할 때
example_1: I’d like to schedule something for next week if that works for you.
example_2: I’d like to schedule a quick call to discuss the details.

translation_ko: 말도 안 돼 / 그럴 확률이 얼마나 돼요?
situation: 우연히 비슷한 일이 겹쳐서 놀랄 때
nuance: 비꼼 없이 놀람/유머가 섞인 구어 톤
example_1: You and I ended up at the same café—what are the odds?
example_2: I ran into my old teacher at the airport. What are the odds?

situation: 상대의 말에 강하게 공감하며 적극적으로 동의할 때
example_1: I couldn’t agree more. That’s exactly what we need.
example_2: I couldn’t agree more—quality matters more than speed.

situation: 상대가 불안해할 때 안심시키며 말해줄 때
example_1: You don’t have to worry. I’ll handle it.
example_2: You don’t have to worry—I’ll make sure it’s ready on time.

situation: 오후에 회의나 업무 연락 시작할 때
example_1: Good afternoon. Are you available for a quick call?
example_2: Good afternoon. Thank you for joining us.

situation: 저녁 시간에 이메일/전화/대면 인사할 때
nuance: 격식을 갖춘 저녁 인사로, 상황에 따라 가볍게 쓸 수 있어요.
example_1: Good evening. I hope you are doing well.
example_2: Good evening. We received your message.

situation: 업무 전에 짧게 안부를 물을 때
nuance: 가벼운 안부 인사로, 너무 길게 대화하지 않아도 자연스러워요.
example_1: Hi! How are you today?
example_2: Hello. How are you? Do you have a minute?

situation: 도움 주거나 답변을 받았을 때
nuance: 가장 기본적인 감사 표현이에요. 짧고 공손합니다.
example_1: Thank you for your help today.
example_2: Thank you. I appreciate your time.

situation: 상대가 말하거나 일을 시작하도록 허락할 때
example_1: Please, go ahead. How can I help?
example_2: Yes, please, go ahead and explain.

situation: 일 처리나 요청이 필요할 때 도움을 부탁할 때
example_1: Could you help me with this document?
example_2: Excuse me—could you help me find the office?

situation: 업무 중 궁금한 점을 물어보고 싶을 때
nuance: 격식 있게 허락을 구하는 질문이라 편안해요.
example_1: Can I ask a question about the schedule?
example_2: Yes, of course. Can I ask a question?

situation: 간단히 바로 질문할 때
nuance: 짧고 자연스러워요. A1 수준에서 자주 써요.
example_1: I have a question about the invoice.
example_2: I have a question. What time is the meeting?

situation: 상대 말을 잘 못 알아들었을 때
nuance: 실례가 되지 않게 솔직히 말하는 공손한 표현이에요.
example_1: Sorry, I don’t understand. Can you say it again?
example_2: Sorry, I don’t understand. What does this mean?

situation: 사무실/문서/물건 위치를 물을 때
nuance: 직설적이지만 업무 상황에서는 매우 흔하고 쉬워요.
example_1: Where is the meeting room?
example_2: Where is the printer?

situation: 문서/업무 결과를 당일로 요청할 때
example_1: I need this today. Is it possible?
example_2: Please send the report today. I need this today.

situation: 회의 시간 안내/확인할 때
example_1: The meeting is at 3:00 in Room 204.
example_2: Okay. The meeting is at 3:00. Thank you.

situation: 회의/약속 시간을 조정해야 할 때
example_1: Can we reschedule our meeting for next week?
example_2: I’m sorry, but can we reschedule? Something came up.

expression: I will send it by email.
situation: 자료/문서를 전달하겠다고 할 때
example_1: I will send it by email today.
example_2: Don’t worry—I will send it by email.

situation: 상대가 이메일을 확인하도록 안내할 때
example_1: Please check your email for the updated file.
example_2: Please check your email. I sent the details.

situation: 문서/자료가 있는지 확인할 때
example_1: Do you have the file for the presentation?
example_2: Hi, do you have the file we need today?

situation: 상대가 파일을 내려받도록 요청/확인할 때
nuance: 기술적으로 아주 쉬운 업무 요청에 자연스러워요.
example_1: Can you download it and send it back?
example_2: Please try to download it. Can you do that?

situation: 서류에 서명 요청할 때
example_1: Could you sign here, please?
example_2: Thank you. Could you sign here and date it?

situation: 이메일에 파일을 첨부하겠다고 말할 때
example_1: I’m attaching the document to this email.
example_2: Don’t worry—I’m attaching the document now.

situation: 문서/자료를 읽고 확인해 달라고 요청할 때
example_1: Please review it and let me know your comments.
example_2: Please review it before the meeting.

expression: Let me know if you have questions.
situation: 상대가 이해 못했거나 궁금할 때 연락하도록 안내할 때
example_1: Let me know if you have questions about the form.
example_2: Thanks again. Let me know if you have questions.

situation: 대화/미팅 후 후속 연락을 예고할 때
example_1: Thank you for your time. We’ll be in touch.
example_2: We’ll be in touch after we review everything.

situation: 업무 통화/대면 후 인사로 마무리할 때
nuance: 밝고 친절한 마무리 인사로 가볍게 쓰기 좋아요.
example_1: Thank you. Have a great day!
example_2: It was nice talking to you. Have a great day!

situation: 회의나 팀 미팅을 시작할 때 인사로 사용해요.
nuance: 정중하고 친근한 톤으로 분위기를 부드럽게 만들어요.
example_1: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining the meeting.
example_2: Good morning, everyone. Let’s get started.

situation: 누군가와 면담/통화 후, 또는 미팅 요청에 동의받았을 때 사용해요.
example_1: Thank you for your time. I really appreciate it.
example_2: Thank you for your time today. Have a great day.

situation: 업무 중에 도움이 필요할 때, 상대에게 요청할 때 사용해요.
example_1: Excuse me, could you please help me with this form?
example_2: Could you please help me find the meeting room?

expression: Let me check that for you
situation: 즉시 답하기 어렵거나 정보를 확인해야 할 때 사용해요.
example_1: Let me check that for you and get back to you shortly.
example_2: I’m not sure yet—let me check that for you.

situation: 확인 후 답을 주겠다고 할 때 사용해요.
example_1: Thanks. I’ll get back to you by tomorrow.
example_2: I can’t confirm now, but I’ll get back to you.

situation: 중요한 사안이나 문제를 같이 이야기해야 할 때 사용해요.
example_1: We need to discuss this issue with the team.
example_2: I think we need to discuss this project plan.

situation: 정보(자료/설명/메일)를 요청할 때 사용해요.
example_1: Please send me the details about the event.
example_2: Could you please send me the details of the budget?

expression: Can you share this with me?
translation_ko: 이것을 저와 공유해 주실 수 있나요?
situation: 문서나 링크 등을 공유해 달라고 할 때 사용해요.
example_1: Can you share this report with me?
example_2: Could you share the link with me?

situation: 문제를 조사하거나 정보를 찾아보는 중이라고 말할 때 사용해요.
example_1: Thanks for your message. I’m looking into it now.
example_2: I’m looking into it and I’ll update you soon.

situation: 긴급도는 있지만 상황에 따라 조정할 수 있을 때 요청/기한을 말해요.
example_1: Please review it and send your feedback as soon as possible.
example_2: We’ll schedule the meeting as soon as possible.

situation: 미팅/약속 시간이 지연될 때 솔직하게 알릴 때 사용해요.
example_1: Sorry, we’re running late. We’ll be there in 10 minutes.
example_2: We’re running late, but we’ll start soon.

situation: 양해를 구하거나 허락을 요청할 때 사용해요.
example_1: Is it okay if I take a quick break?
example_2: Is it okay if I join the call a few minutes late?

situation: 약속/정보를 재확인할 때 사용해요.
example_1: I’d like to confirm the meeting time.
example_2: I’d like to confirm your address.

situation: 회의 시간/장소를 알릴 때 사용해요.
example_1: The meeting is at 2:00 PM in Room 3.
example_2: The meeting is at 10:30. Please be there early.

situation: 상대 말이 잘 들리지 않았을 때 다시 요청할 때 사용해요.
nuance: 예의 있고 차분하게 말할 수 있어요.
example_1: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
example_2: Could you repeat that again? I didn’t catch it.

situation: 상대 의견에 동의할 때 사용해요.
example_1: I agree with you. We should move forward.
example_2: I agree with you about the next steps.

situation: 상대의 의견을 물어볼 때 사용해요.
example_1: How do you think about this idea?
example_2: How do you think we should handle the problem?

situation: 자료나 문서를 함께 확인하자고 할 때 사용해요.
example_1: Let’s take a look at the document together.
example_2: We should take a look at the numbers first.

situation: 추가로 연락하거나 진행 상황을 점검하겠다고 말할 때 사용해요.
example_1: Don’t worry—we’ll follow up with you tomorrow.
example_2: We’ll follow up after the meeting with the final details.

situation: 상대가 정보를 주거나 결과를 공유해 주길 요청할 때 사용해요.
example_1: Please let me know if you need anything else.
example_2: Please let me know the result when you can.

situation: 미팅/통화를 제안하거나 가능 일정을 말할 때 사용해요.
example_1: I’m available tomorrow morning. Does that work for you?
example_2: I’m available tomorrow after 2 PM.

situation: 약속 시간이 어려워서 미팅 시간을 바꾸고 싶을 때 사용해요.
example_1: Sorry, I have a conflict. Could we reschedule?
example_2: Could we reschedule the meeting to next week?

situation: 파일/서류를 전달하거나 공유할 때 사용해요.
example_1: Here are the documents for your review.
example_2: Here are the documents you requested.

situation: 결정/허가를 받기 전 진행 상황을 설명할 때 사용해요.
example_1: We’re waiting for approval from the manager.
example_2: The project is on hold—we’re waiting for approval.

situation: 결재/승인이 완료되었을 때 결과를 공유할 때 사용해요.
example_1: Great news—the budget has been approved.
example_2: The budget has been approved, so we can start now.

situation: 상대와 직접 만나 논의하자고 제안할 때 사용해요.
example_1: I think we should meet in person to discuss the details.
example_2: We should meet in person if that’s possible.

expression: Could we schedule a quick call?
translation_ko: 짧게 통화 일정을 잡을 수 있을까요?
situation: 업무 논의를 위해 짧은 통화를 제안할 때
example_1: Could we schedule a quick call to discuss the timeline?
example_2: I’m free this afternoon—could we schedule a quick call?

expression: I’d like to follow up on this.
translation_ko: 이 건에 대해 후속으로 확인하고 싶습니다.
situation: 이전에 이야기한 내용의 진행 상황을 물을 때
example_1: I’d like to follow up on the proposal we discussed last week.
example_2: Could you let me know the status? I’d like to follow up on this matter.

expression: Thanks for your time and support.
situation: 회의나 요청에 대한 감사 인사로 마무리할 때
example_1: Thanks for your time and support during the meeting.
example_2: Thanks for your time and support. I really appreciate it.

expression: Please let me know if anything changes.
situation: 향후 일정/조건이 바뀔 수 있음을 전제로 확인할 때
nuance: 배려 있는 톤, 상황 파악을 요청
example_1: Please let me know if anything changes on your side.
example_2: We’ll wait for your confirmation—please let me know if anything changes.

expression: We should keep things on track.
translation_ko: 일정이 차질 없이 진행되도록 해야 합니다.
situation: 프로젝트 진행을 점검하며 일정 준수를 강조할 때
example_1: Let’s review priorities so we can keep things on track.
example_2: To avoid delays, we should keep things on track this week.

translation_ko: 내일 한번 간단히 다시 이야기해 볼까요?
situation: 짧게 상태를 확인하기 위해 재연락 약속을 잡을 때
nuance: 자연스럽고 가벼운 업무 톤(격식 있지만 편안함)
example_1: Let’s touch base tomorrow morning and see where things stand.
example_2: I’ll send you an update today, and we can touch base tomorrow.

situation: 이전에 합의한 내용대로 다음 단계를 시작할 때
example_1: As discussed, we’ll move forward with the revised plan.
example_2: As discussed, we’ll move forward with the next phase next week.

expression: Could you share the latest update?
translation_ko: 최신 진행 상황을 공유해 주실 수 있을까요?
situation: 업데이트가 필요하지만 자료가 최신인지 확인할 때
example_1: Could you share the latest update on the project status?
example_2: I haven’t seen the newest version yet—could you share the latest update?

expression: We’re aiming to meet the deadline.
translation_ko: 마감 기한을 맞추는 것을 목표로 하고 있습니다.
situation: 일정에 대한 계획/의지를 말할 때
example_1: We’re aiming to meet the deadline, even though the scope changed.
example_2: Our team is working hard to meet the deadline.

expression: I’m afraid that won’t be possible.
situation: 요청을 거절해야 할 때, 직접적 거절을 완화할 때
example_1: I’m afraid that won’t be possible due to scheduling constraints.
example_2: I’m afraid that won’t be possible this week, but we can try next week.

situation: 상대의 제안을 동의할 때 가볍게 반응할 때
example_1: That sounds good to me. Let’s proceed.
example_2: If it works for you, that sounds good to me.

expression: Do you have a few minutes?
situation: 짧게 대화를 요청할 때
example_1: Do you have a few minutes to review the document with me?
example_2: Do you have a few minutes after the meeting?

expression: Let me check and get back to you.
situation: 즉답이 어려워 확인 후 회신할 때
nuance: 책임감 있고 시간 여유를 주는 톤
example_1: Let me check and get back to you by 3 PM.
example_2: Thanks—let me check and get back to you shortly.

expression: We need to align on priorities.
situation: 팀/부서 간 기대를 조율할 때
example_1: Before we start, we need to align on priorities.
example_2: Let’s align on priorities so everyone is working toward the same goal.

translation_ko: 세부 사항을 확인해 주실 수 있을까요?
situation: 정보가 불확실할 때 확인을 요청할 때
example_1: Could you confirm the details of the meeting time and location?
example_2: I want to make sure I have everything right—could you confirm the details?

situation: 프로세스 진행 순서를 확인할 때
example_1: What’s the next step after we review the draft?
example_2: Once the approval is done, what’s the next step?

situation: 의견/승인을 기다리는 동안 진행 상황을 말할 때
example_1: We’re currently reviewing your proposal and will respond soon.
example_2: The team is reviewing it now; we’ll share feedback by Friday.

expression: Let’s discuss this in more detail.
translation_ko: 이것을 좀 더 자세히 논의해 봅시다.
situation: 간단히 말한 뒤 추가 설명이 필요할 때
example_1: I think we need to discuss this in more detail to avoid misunderstandings.
example_2: Let’s discuss this in more detail during the next meeting.

situation: 승인 단계가 남아 있어 진행이 멈춰 있을 때 알릴 때
example_1: We’re waiting for your approval before we proceed.
example_2: Once we receive your approval, we can move forward immediately.

expression: Please keep me in the loop.
situation: 업무 관련 최신 정보를 공유받고 싶을 때
nuance: 친근하지만 직장 내에서 자주 쓰는 톤
example_1: Please keep me in the loop about any changes to the schedule.
example_2: I’d appreciate it if you could keep me in the loop on progress.

expression: I can’t access that from here.
situation: 권한/접속 문제로 자료를 열 수 없을 때
example_1: I can’t access that from here—could you send the link?
example_2: I can’t access the file from my account. Could you check permissions?

translation_ko: 제가 이해한 게 맞는지 잘 모르겠어요.
situation: 개념이나 지시가 불명확할 때 확인 요청할 때
example_1: I’m not sure I understand—could you explain it again?
example_2: I’m not sure I understand your point. Could you give an example?

situation: 예상치 못한 오류/장애가 발생했을 때 보고할 때
example_1: We’ve run into an issue with the data upload.
example_2: Just a heads-up—we’ve run into an issue and are investigating.

situation: 회의 시작 전에 순서를 확인할 때
example_1: Before we start, let’s review the agenda for today.
example_2: Let’s review the agenda quickly so we can stay on time.

expression: I’ll send you the file shortly.
situation: 자료를 곧 전달하겠다고 할 때
example_1: I’ll send you the file shortly after I finalize it.
example_2: Thanks for your patience—I’ll send you the file shortly.

expression: We need to document this decision.
situation: 향후 참고/감사를 위해 결정사항을 기록할 때
example_1: We need to document this decision for future reference.
example_2: Let’s make sure we document this decision in the meeting notes.

translation_ko: 숫자는 한 번 더 확인해 주세요.
situation: 계산/수치 오류를 방지하기 위해 재검토를 요청할 때
example_1: Please double-check the numbers before you submit the report.
example_2: I recommend double-checking the figures to avoid mistakes.

expression: We’ll schedule it for next week.
situation: 향후 회의/업무 일정을 정하고 확정할 때
example_1: We’ll schedule it for next week and send a calendar invite.
example_2: If that works, we’ll schedule it for next week.

expression: Could you provide a brief summary?
situation: 긴 문서/보고서 내용을 핵심만 알고 싶을 때
example_1: Could you provide a brief summary of the key findings?
example_2: I don’t have time to read everything—could you provide a brief summary?

situation: 의견을 말할 때(회의, 보고, 논의) 자신의 관점을 부드럽게 제시할 때
nuance: 단정적이지 않게 말하는 완곡한 표현(상대가 반대해도 부담이 적음)
example_1: From my perspective, we should prioritize customer feedback this quarter.
example_2: From my perspective, the timeline is still realistic if we add one more reviewer.

situation: 핵심 포인트를 말할 때(발표, 이메일, 회의에서 결론 전 강조)
nuance: 공식적이고 정중한 톤으로 발표/보고의 흐름을 잡아줌
example_1: I’d like to highlight the main risks we identified during the assessment.
example_2: I’d like to highlight that the new process reduced turnaround time by 20%.

situation: 막연한 말을 구체화할 때(설명, 질문, 회의에서 후속 설명)
example_1: To be more specific, the budget includes staffing and software licenses.
example_2: To be more specific, we need confirmation from the finance team by Friday.

situation: 받아들이기 어려운 소식/거절/부정적 정보를 전달할 때
nuance: 완곡하고 공손한 유감/거절 표현(직접적인 거절을 완화)
example_1: I’m afraid that we won’t be able to meet the original deadline.
example_2: I’m afraid that the current version doesn’t support that feature.

situation: 불명확한 부분을 확인할 때(회의, 이메일, 요청 답변)
example_1: Could you clarify what you mean by “ongoing maintenance”?
example_2: Could you clarify the approval process for expense reports?

situation: 장점/의견을 말한 뒤 조건·단점을 덧붙일 때(균형 잡힌 발언)
nuance: 앞에서 말한 내용을 완화하거나 방향을 조정하는 말
example_1: The proposal is strong. That said, we need more details on costs.
example_2: The first draft looks good. That said, I’d like to adjust the timeline.

situation: 진행 상황을 기준으로 말할 때(초기/중간/마무리 단계 설명)
nuance: 시점 제한을 분명히 하는 신중한 표현
example_1: At this stage, we’re still validating the assumptions.
example_2: At this stage, it would be risky to commit to a fixed date.

situation: 목적/의도를 설명할 때(계획, 문서, 이메일)
nuance: 격식 있는 표현으로 B2에서 자주 쓰임
example_1: We’re meeting today in order to finalize the scope.
example_2: In order to reduce delays, we need earlier access to the files.

situation: 프로젝트가 늦어졌음을 보고할 때(진척 공유, 리스크 알림)
nuance: 문제 상황을 사실적으로 전달하되 개선 의지가 함께 필요
example_1: We’re running behind schedule, so we’ll need to adjust the next milestones.
example_2: We’re running behind schedule, but we’re already taking steps to catch up.

situation: 논쟁이 꼬였거나 방향을 재정비할 필요가 있을 때
nuance: 긴장을 완화하고 재검토를 유도하는 유연한 표현
example_1: Let’s take a step back and review the requirements once more.
example_2: The discussion is getting stuck—let’s take a step back.

situation: 말의 결론을 정리할 때(회의 마무리, 발표 마지막)
example_1: To sum up, we will launch the pilot in September.
example_2: To sum up, the key issue is customer communication.

situation: 다음 행동을 약속할 때(이메일, 회의 종료 후 후속 조치)
example_1: Thanks for your time. I’ll follow up with the updated report tomorrow.
example_2: I’ll follow up with HR regarding your request.

situation: 의견/기준/방향을 맞출 필요가 있을 때(전략, 목표, 요구사항)
nuance: 팀 의사결정에 초점이 있는 실무적인 톤
example_1: We need to align on the success metrics before we start development.
example_2: Let’s align on how we’ll handle scope changes.

situation: 필수 조건/주의 사항을 전달할 때(지시, 체크리스트, 품질 관리)
nuance: 요구가 강해질 수 있어 상황에 따라 정중하게 다듬기 좋음
example_1: Make sure that all documents are submitted by 5 p.m.
example_2: Make sure that the client receives the final version today.

expression: I have a couple of questions
situation: 회의나 연락에서 가볍게 질문을 시작할 때
example_1: I have a couple of questions about the proposed budget.
example_2: I have a couple of questions regarding the project timeline.

situation: 대안이나 개선 방안을 제안할 때(회의, 계획 수립)
example_1: We should consider reducing the scope to meet the deadline.
example_2: We should consider adding a testing phase before rollout.

translation_ko: 급할 건 아니에요 / 서두를 필요는 없어요
situation: 상대에게 시간 압박을 주지 않으려 할 때(응답 지연, 일정 조율)
example_1: There’s no rush—please review it when you have time.
example_2: There’s no rush. We can discuss this next week.

situation: 협조/지원에 감사를 표현할 때(이메일, 대화)
example_1: I appreciate your help with the presentation materials.
example_2: I appreciate your help in resolving the issue quickly.

situation: 수치/일정/결과를 전망할 때(리포트, 계획 공유)
example_1: We’re expecting the final approval by the end of next week.
example_2: We’re expecting a gradual improvement in performance after the update.

situation: 회의/문서의 핵심 메시지를 정리할 때
example_1: The main takeaway is that we need clearer ownership for each task.
example_2: The main takeaway is that customer communication drives retention.

situation: 의사결정/진행을 위해 상대의 승인 요청할 때
nuance: 업무 절차를 분명히 하는 공식 톤
example_1: We’ll need your approval before we finalize the contract.
example_2: We’ll need your approval to proceed with the new vendor.

situation: 조건에 따라 달라진다고 답할 때(질문에 대한 반응)
nuance: 회피가 아니라 합리적 조건을 제시하는 표현
example_1: That depends on whether we can secure additional resources.
example_2: That depends on the timing of the client’s feedback.

situation: 간단한 논의를 위해 미팅 대신 콜을 제안할 때
nuance: 간편하고 실용적인 제안 톤(관계 친밀도에도 무난)
example_1: Let’s schedule a quick call to confirm next steps.
example_2: Let’s schedule a quick call this afternoon if that works for you.

situation: 원인과 결과를 연결해 설명할 때(분석, 보고서, 회의)
nuance: 논리 흐름을 만드는 공식적인 연결 표현
example_1: As a result, we reduced customer complaints by 15%.
example_2: As a result of the change, the delivery timeline improved.

situation: 승인/합의 후 다음 단계로 넘어갈 때
example_1: Once we receive the approval, we can move forward with the implementation.
example_2: After aligning on the scope, we can move forward with the design phase.

expression: to be on the same page
translation_ko: 같은 입장에 있다 / 같은 내용을 이해하고 있다
situation: 회의 전후에 모두가 동일한 목표·내용을 이해했는지 확인할 때
example_1: Before we finalize the proposal, let’s make sure we’re on the same page about the scope.
example_2: I think we’re on the same page regarding timelines, but I’d like to confirm the next steps.

situation: 여러 팀이 해야 할 일의 우선순위를 맞출 때
nuance: 전략적 조율과 실무 합의를 담은 톤
example_1: Let’s align on priorities for this quarter so everyone can plan effectively.
example_2: We held a short meeting to align on priorities before starting the sprint.

situation: 요구사항이 바뀌거나 진행 중 이슈가 생겨 범위를 재조정해야 할 때
example_1: Given the new requirements, we may need to revisit the scope and timeline.
example_2: I’d like to revisit the scope to ensure we’re not overcommitting.

situation: 기존 계획이 비효율적일 때 대안을 제시할 때
example_1: If the current plan is too risky, I’d propose an alternative approach.
example_2: We can propose an alternative approach that reduces turnaround time without sacrificing quality.

situation: 리스크·문제점을 조심스럽게 알릴 때
example_1: I’d like to raise a concern about the assumptions behind the forecast.
example_2: Please don’t hesitate to raise a concern if anything looks off.

situation: 이미 확인된 문제에 대해 구체적으로 조치할 때
example_1: We’re addressing the issue by strengthening our review process.
example_2: Let’s address the issue first, then discuss how to prevent it from recurring.

expression: to take ownership of a task
situation: 특정 역할을 본인이 주도적으로 수행하겠다고 할 때
example_1: I’ll take ownership of the reporting process and deliver the first draft by Friday.
example_2: To move faster, we should each take ownership of our respective tasks.

situation: 일정 관리, 납기 준수 여부를 말할 때
example_1: We’re on track to meet the deadline, barring any unexpected delays.
example_2: We may need additional resources to meet the deadline confidently.

situation: 결과·기간·범위에 대해 현실적으로 조정할 때
nuance: 상황을 설명하며 혼란을 줄이는 신중한 톤
example_1: To manage expectations, the timeline depends on third-party approvals.
example_2: I want to manage expectations by clarifying what’s included in the first phase.

situation: 법규·내부 정책·규정 준수 관련 업무에서
example_1: We’re introducing new controls to ensure compliance with data privacy requirements.
example_2: Please ensure compliance by following the company’s procurement guidelines.

situation: 문서·프로세스·결과를 신중하게 점검할 때
example_1: Before signing off, we will conduct a thorough review of the financial statements.
example_2: I recommend conducting a thorough review of the customer feedback before acting.

situation: 정기 회의나 보고에서 현재 상태를 공유할 때
example_1: Here’s a quick status update on the project timeline and key risks.
example_2: Could you provide a status update on the tasks assigned to your team?

situation: 기획/분석 단계에서 필요 조건을 파악할 때
example_1: Our first step is to gather requirements from stakeholders across departments.
example_2: We’re currently gathering requirements to ensure the solution fits real workflows.

situation: 업무 절차를 더 효율적으로 만들기 위해 개선할 때
example_1: We streamlined the process to reduce processing time by 30%.
example_2: Let’s look at where we can streamline the approval workflow.

situation: 비용 절감 프로젝트나 재무 목표를 설명할 때
example_1: The new vendor contract helped us reduce operational costs significantly.
example_2: We’re exploring options to reduce operational costs without impacting quality.

situation: 불확실성이나 잠재 문제를 줄이기 위한 대책을 말할 때
example_1: We can mitigate risk by adding an additional review step before launch.
example_2: Our contingency plan is designed to mitigate risk in case of delays.

situation: 중장기 계획, 실행 계획을 단계별로 제시할 때
example_1: Let’s develop a roadmap that outlines milestones for the next six months.
example_2: We’ll use the roadmap to align teams on deliverables and timing.

situation: 여러 대안 중 최선의 방안을 비교·판단할 때
example_1: We’re evaluating options to determine the most cost-effective solution.
example_2: Before choosing a vendor, we need to evaluate options based on performance and support.

situation: 계약/일정/기획에서 마지막 조율 단계일 때
example_1: We’re close to finalizing the details of the contract and timeline.
example_2: Once we finalize details, we can share the plan with the broader team.

situation: 상급자/위원회로부터 공식 결정을 받아야 할 때
example_1: I’d like to seek approval for the budget adjustment before Friday.
example_2: We need to seek approval from legal prior to sending the agreement.

translation_ko: 공감을 얻고 지지를 확보하다 / 동의를 끌어내다
situation: 프로젝트가 성공하려면 이해관계자 동의가 필요할 때
example_1: We need to obtain buy-in from key stakeholders before we proceed.
example_2: To obtain buy-in, we explained the benefits and addressed their concerns early.

situation: 협업 시작 전 역할·결과물을 분명히 할 때
example_1: Let’s set clear expectations for deliverables, quality, and turnaround time.
example_2: When we set clear expectations, teams move faster with fewer misunderstandings.

situation: 고객/협력사/내부 부서와의 관계를 지속적으로 관리할 때
example_1: Part of my role is to manage a stakeholder relationship across product and operations.
example_2: Effective stakeholder relationship management helped us resolve issues quickly.

situation: 성과·업무 진행에서 책임 소재를 분명히 할 때
example_1: We introduced clear owners for each deliverable to ensure accountability.
example_2: To ensure accountability, we defined roles and reporting lines from the start.

situation: 회의/워크숍에서 경험을 바탕으로 팁을 나눌 때
example_1: During the session, we shared best practices for improving customer onboarding.
example_2: I’m happy to share best practices from our previous projects if that’s helpful.

situation: 프로젝트 중간에 지연 없이 계속 추진하려 할 때
example_1: After the kickoff, we focused on maintaining momentum with weekly check-ins.
example_2: Let’s keep the schedule moving to maintain momentum through the final phase.

situation: KPI/마일스톤 기반으로 실제 진행을 모니터링할 때
example_1: We track progress using a dashboard updated every Monday.
example_2: Could you track progress on your tasks and flag any blockers early?

situation: 보고서/제안서에서 단순한 의견이 아니라 구체적 제안을 할 때
example_1: The audit report includes actionable recommendations to improve compliance.
example_2: Based on the analysis, I’d like to provide actionable recommendations for the next quarter.

expression: We need to align on priorities for this quarter
translation_ko: 이번 분기 우선순위에 대해 합의할 필요가 있습니다
situation: 분기/기간 계획을 논의할 때, 팀 간 목표와 순서를 맞출 때
nuance: 구체적인 합의가 필요하다는 점을 부드럽게 강조하는 톤
example_1: Before we start, we need to align on priorities for this quarter so everyone is working toward the same goals.
example_2: Let’s align on priorities for this quarter during the next meeting and confirm the timeline.

expression: I’d like to follow up on our previous conversation
translation_ko: 지난 대화에 대해 후속으로 말씀드리고 싶습니다
situation: 이메일/회의 후 답변이나 진행 상황을 이어서 전달할 때
nuance: 예의 바르고 공식적인 후속 커뮤니케이션 톤
example_1: I’d like to follow up on our previous conversation about the vendor selection process.
example_2: Thanks for your time—I'd like to follow up on the action items we discussed last week.

expression: Could you share your recommendations on next steps?
translation_ko: 다음 단계에 대한 제안(권고)을 공유해 주실 수 있을까요?
situation: 의사결정이나 진행 방향을 정하기 전에 상대의 의견을 요청할 때
nuance: 상대의 전문성을 존중하며 의견을 구하는 공손한 톤
example_1: Could you share your recommendations on next steps based on the current data?
example_2: Once you’ve reviewed the report, could you share your recommendations on next steps for the project?

expression: Let’s move forward with the proposed approach
situation: 검토가 끝났거나 합의가 된 후 실제 실행을 시작할 때
nuance: 결정하고 실행으로 옮기는 단호하지만 협조적인 톤
example_1: If there are no further concerns, let’s move forward with the proposed approach.
example_2: After reviewing the risks, we decided to move forward with the proposed approach.

expression: I’m concerned about potential risks in the timeline
situation: 지연/리스크가 예상될 때 우려를 공식적으로 제기할 때
nuance: 문제 제기이되 과도하게 공격적이지 않은 신중한 톤
example_1: I’m concerned about potential risks in the timeline if we don’t finalize requirements this week.
example_2: We can manage costs, but I’m concerned about potential risks in the timeline for the launch.

expression: From a strategic standpoint, this makes sense
situation: 의사결정에서 큰 그림(전략) 근거를 제시할 때
nuance: 논리적이고 설득력 있는, 상위 관점의 톤
example_1: From a strategic standpoint, this makes sense because it strengthens our core capabilities.
example_2: Even though it’s costly upfront, from a strategic standpoint, this makes sense for long-term growth.

expression: We should ensure alignment across stakeholders
situation: 여러 부서/파트너가 얽힌 프로젝트에서 역할과 기대를 맞출 때
nuance: 누락을 방지하고 조율 필요성을 강조하는 신중한 톤
example_1: To avoid rework, we should ensure alignment across stakeholders before we begin implementation.
example_2: We’ll set up weekly checkpoints to ensure alignment across stakeholders throughout the rollout.

expression: This will require a coordinated effort
situation: 개인 업무를 넘어 여러 팀이 협업해야 할 때
example_1: Improving the onboarding experience will require a coordinated effort across product and support.
example_2: To meet the deadline, this will require a coordinated effort from every involved team.

situation: 권한/담당이 불분명할 때, 작업 분배를 정리할 때
nuance: 문제를 정확히 짚고 체계를 세우는 실무 톤
example_1: Before the next sprint, let’s clarify roles and responsibilities to prevent confusion.
example_2: We should clarify roles and responsibilities for approvals, reporting, and escalation.

expression: I recommend we conduct a thorough review
situation: 결정 전에 점검이 필요할 때(감사, 검토, 리스크 평가 등)
example_1: I recommend we conduct a thorough review of the requirements before committing resources.
example_2: Given the complexity, I recommend we conduct a thorough review with the relevant teams.

expression: Please keep me posted on your progress
situation: 상대가 작업을 수행하는 동안 업데이트를 요청할 때
example_1: Please keep me posted on your progress with the integration testing.
example_2: If anything changes, please keep me posted on your progress regarding the deliverables.

expression: We’re operating under a tight deadline
translation_ko: 우리는 촉박한 마감 기한 하에 진행하고 있습니다
situation: 시간 압박이 있을 때 계획 조정이나 우선순위 재조정을 설명할 때
nuance: 현실을 공유하고 기대치 조정을 암시하는 톤
example_1: We’re operating under a tight deadline, so we may need to prioritize the critical items first.
example_2: Because we’re operating under a tight deadline, please flag any blockers as soon as possible.

expression: Could you confirm receipt of this message?
translation_ko: 이 메시지 수신을 확인해 주실 수 있을까요?
situation: 중요한 이메일/문서를 보낸 뒤 확인을 요청할 때
example_1: Could you confirm receipt of this message so we can proceed with the next step?
example_2: Please confirm receipt of the contract by end of day.

expression: We need to ensure compliance with policy requirements
situation: 법무/컴플라이언스/내부 정책 관련 확인이 필요할 때
nuance: 규정 준수의 중요성을 강조하는 엄격한 톤
example_1: We need to ensure compliance with policy requirements before we share customer data.
example_2: As part of the process, we’ll document how each decision aligns with compliance requirements.

expression: Let’s address this gap before it escalates
translation_ko: 이 문제가 확대되기 전에 그 공백(차이)을 해결합시다
situation: 리스크/오해/차이가 커질 조짐이 있을 때 조기 조치할 때
example_1: Let’s address this gap before it escalates and affects the deliverable timeline.
example_2: If we don’t address this gap now, it could escalate during the audit.

expression: I want to make sure we’re on the same page
translation_ko: 우리가 같은 이해를 하고 있는지 확인하고 싶습니다
situation: 회의/협의에서 오해를 방지하거나 기준을 맞출 때
example_1: Before we finalize the scope, I want to make sure we’re on the same page about the requirements.
example_2: I want to make sure we’re on the same page regarding success metrics for the project.

expression: This is outside my scope of responsibility
situation: 권한/업무 범위가 아닐 때 정중하게 선을 긋고 조정할 때
nuance: 단호하지만 예의 있는 톤(회피가 아니라 경계 설정)
example_1: This is outside my scope of responsibility, but I can connect you with the right owner.
example_2: I can’t directly handle that task because it’s outside my scope of responsibility.

situation: 현재 계획이 불확실할 때 플랜B/대안을 논의할 때
example_1: We should consider alternative options if the current vendor can’t meet the turnaround time.
example_2: Let’s document the assumptions and consider alternative options before making a final call.

expression: The current proposal aligns with our objectives
translation_ko: 현재 제안은 우리의 목표와 잘 맞습니다
situation: 제안/안이 목표에 부합함을 긍정적으로 평가할 때
nuance: 인정과 지지의 톤, 설득력 있게 마무리하는 느낌
example_1: After comparing the proposals, the current proposal aligns with our objectives for scalability and cost control.
example_2: The timeline in the current proposal aligns with our operational targets.

expression: I’ll take the lead on this task
situation: 책임을 맡고 실행을 진행하겠다고 할 때
nuance: 주도권을 명확히 밝히는 책임감 있는 톤
example_1: I’ll take the lead on this task and share progress updates every two days.
example_2: If you’re comfortable with it, I’ll take the lead on this task to keep things moving.

expression: We need to manage expectations proactively
situation: 상대가 현실적인 범위를 이해하도록 미리 조정해야 할 때
example_1: We need to manage expectations proactively so stakeholders understand what’s feasible by the deadline.
example_2: By clarifying assumptions early, we can manage expectations proactively and reduce escalations.

situation: 단순한 이슈가 아니라 파급효과가 큰 결정을 설명할 때
nuance: 중요성과 신중함을 드러내는 격식 있는 톤
example_1: This decision has far-reaching implications for our compliance posture and long-term operations.
example_2: We should evaluate how this change impacts stakeholders because this decision has far-reaching implications.

expression: Let’s ensure the data is consistent and reliable
translation_ko: 데이터가 일관되고 신뢰할 수 있는지 확인합시다
situation: 분석/보고에서 데이터 품질을 점검할 때
example_1: Before we draw conclusions, let’s ensure the data is consistent and reliable across all sources.
example_2: We’ll validate the dataset to ensure the data is consistent and reliable for the final report.

expression: We need to prioritize quality over speed
situation: 급하게 진행 중 실수/리스크가 커질 때 품질을 강조하며 방향을 조정할 때
nuance: 현실적인 균형을 조언하는 단호하지만 건설적인 톤
example_1: Given the stakes, we need to prioritize quality over speed to avoid costly rework.
example_2: I agree we’re under time pressure, but we need to prioritize quality over speed for this deliverable.

expression: Please provide your input by COB tomorrow
translation_ko: 내일까지 업무종료(COB) 시간까지 의견을 주시기 바랍니다
situation: 기한이 정해진 피드백/검토 요청을 할 때
nuance: 업무 현장의 관행을 반영한 실무적이고 간결한 톤
example_1: Please provide your input by COB tomorrow so we can finalize the slide deck.
example_2: Can you review the draft and provide your input by COB tomorrow?

expression: I’d like to schedule a brief check-in
situation: 정기 미팅/업데이트를 위한 짧은 일정 조율을 할 때
nuance: 부담을 줄이면서도 진행을 지속하려는 친근한 공식 톤
example_1: I’d like to schedule a brief check-in to review the status and unblock any issues.
example_2: Let’s schedule a brief check-in on Thursday to confirm next steps.

expression: We should document decisions for future reference
translation_ko: 향후 참고를 위해 결정을 문서로 남겨야 합니다
situation: 회의 후 결정 사항/근거를 기록해야 할 때(감사, 인수인계)
example_1: To ensure transparency, we should document decisions for future reference.
example_2: After the meeting, please capture the rationale so we can document decisions for future reference.

expression: Let’s review the full scope and assumptions
situation: 요구사항/스코프를 재정의하거나 합의 기반을 점검할 때
nuance: 누락 방지를 강조하며 논리적으로 접근하는 톤
example_1: Before we estimate the cost, let’s review the full scope and assumptions with the stakeholders.
example_2: Let’s review the full scope and assumptions to ensure everyone agrees on what’s included.

expression: I’m happy to provide additional context if needed
situation: 상대가 이해를 더 돕기 위해 질문하거나 불확실할 때
example_1: I’m happy to provide additional context if needed—feel free to ask questions about the methodology.
example_2: If you need more detail on the forecast, I’m happy to provide additional context if needed.

expression: We’ll need sign-off from the relevant owners
situation: 최종 승인/권한 확인이 필요한 의사결정 단계에서
nuance: 절차를 강조하며 다음 액션을 명확히 하는 톤
example_1: Before we proceed, we’ll need sign-off from the relevant owners to ensure accountability.
example_2: Can you confirm who the relevant owners are for sign-off on this change request?

expression: To summarize, our main takeaway is that…
situation: 회의/보고에서 결론을 정리하며 발표를 마무리할 때
example_1: To summarize, our main takeaway is that we can reduce risk by tightening the acceptance criteria.
example_2: To summarize, our main takeaway is that the proposed timeline is feasible with the current staffing plan.

expression: Where is the airport bus stop?
situation: 공항에 도착했을 때 버스를 타러 길을 물을 때
example_1: Excuse me, where is the airport bus stop?
example_2: I’m looking for the airport bus stop. Where is it?

expression: I would like a table for two.
situation: 식당에서 자리를 요청할 때
nuance: 정중한 요청, 인원 수를 명확히 말함
example_1: Hello, I would like a table for two, please.
example_2: I would like a table for two at 7 p.m.

situation: 식당에서 음식 종류를 확인할 때
nuance: 다양한 음식 가능성을 정중히 묻는 말
example_1: Do you have vegetarian food?
example_2: I’m vegetarian. Do you have vegetarian food?

situation: 식당에서 음료 주문할 때
example_1: I’ll have water, please.
example_2: Can I get water, please? I’ll have water.

expression: Do you have any specials today?
situation: 식당에서 오늘의 추천/세일 메뉴를 물을 때
example_1: Do you have any specials today?
example_2: Is there a special today? Do you have any specials today?

situation: 알레르기 정보를 알릴 때(안전 관련)
example_1: I’m allergic to peanuts. Is there any peanut in this?
example_2: Please be careful—I’m allergic to peanuts.

situation: 호텔에 도착해서 체크인을 할 때
example_1: Hello, I’d like to check in.
example_2: I’d like to check in, please. I have a reservation.

situation: 호텔에서 퇴실 시간을 확인할 때
example_1: What time is check-out?
example_2: Sorry, what time is check-out tomorrow?

situation: 호텔 요금/패키지에 조식이 포함인지 확인할 때
nuance: 비용 포함 여부를 묻는 공손한 질문
example_1: Is breakfast included in the price?
example_2: Is breakfast included? I’d like to know.

situation: 호텔/건물에서 층 이동을 할 때
nuance: 간단하고 자주 쓰는 길 안내 질문
example_1: Where is the elevator?
example_2: Excuse me, where is the elevator to the second floor?

translation_ko: 수건 하나 더 주실 수 있어요?
situation: 호텔에서 추가로 물품을 요청할 때
example_1: Excuse me, I need an extra towel.
example_2: Can I have an extra towel, please?

situation: 호텔 방 온도가 마음에 들지 않을 때
example_1: The room is too cold. Can you help?
example_2: I think the room temperature is too low.

situation: 호텔에서 와이파이 비밀번호를 확인/안내받을 때
example_1: The Wi-Fi password is written here. What is it?
example_2: Thanks. The Wi-Fi password is on the card.

expression: I’m lost. Can you help me?
situation: 도시에서 길을 잃었을 때 안내를 요청할 때
example_1: I’m lost. Can you help me, please?
example_2: Sorry, I’m lost. Can you help me find this place?

expression: How do I get to the city center?
situation: 도시 중심지로 가는 방법을 물을 때
example_1: How do I get to the city center?
example_2: Excuse me, how do I get to the city center by bus?

situation: 장소가 가까운지 확인할 때
example_1: Is it near here?
example_2: Is the museum near here?

expression: Turn left at the traffic light.
situation: 길 안내를 들을 때(지시를 이해해야 할 때)
example_1: Turn left at the traffic light, and it’s on the right.
example_2: First, turn left at the traffic light.

expression: Turn right at the next street.
situation: 길 안내를 받을 때 다음 방향을 말해줄 때
example_1: Turn right at the next street.
example_2: Go straight, then turn right at the next street.

situation: 정확한 이동 거리를 안내받을 때
example_1: Go straight for two blocks, then stop at the bank.
example_2: Please go straight for two blocks and turn left.

situation: 공항에서 출발/도착 터미널을 찾을 때
nuance: 공항 상황에서 바로 쓰기 좋은 질문
example_1: Where is terminal 2? My flight is there.
example_2: Excuse me, where is terminal 2?

situation: 공항에서 수속을 하러 갈 때
example_1: Where is the check-in counter for my airline?
example_2: Excuse me, where is the check-in counter?

expression: I need help with my luggage.
situation: 공항/호텔에서 짐 관련 도움을 요청할 때
example_1: I need help with my luggage, please.
example_2: Can you help me with my luggage?

situation: 공항 도착 후 짐을 찾으러 갈 때
example_1: I’m looking for baggage claim. Where is it?
example_2: Excuse me, I’m looking for baggage claim.

situation: 출발 시간을 확인할 때
example_1: What time is my flight?
example_2: Can you tell me what time my flight leaves?

situation: 공항이나 호텔에서 체크인할 때 길을 물어볼 때
example_1: Excuse me, where is the check-in desk?
example_2: I can't find the check-in desk. Where is it?

expression: How much is it per night?
situation: 호텔 가격을 물을 때
example_1: How much is it per night?
example_2: Can you tell me how much it is per night?

expression: Can I have a window seat?
situation: 비행기에서 좌석을 요청할 때
example_1: Can I have a window seat, please?
example_2: If possible, I’d like a window seat.

situation: 비행기 탑승 시간을 확인할 때
example_1: What time is boarding for flight 204?
example_2: Excuse me, what time is boarding?

situation: 공항에서 탑승구를 찾을 때
nuance: 구체적인 번호를 넣어 정확히 묻는 표현
example_1: Where is Gate number 12?
example_2: Excuse me, where is Gate number 5?

situation: 호텔 주변이나 위치 근처에서 식당을 찾을 때
nuance: 여유 있게 추천을 받을 수 있는 질문
example_1: Is there a restaurant nearby?
example_2: Do you know any good restaurants nearby?

expression: Do you have a menu in English?
situation: 레스토랑에서 영어 메뉴를 요청할 때
example_1: Do you have a menu in English, please?
example_2: Excuse me, do you have a menu in English?

situation: 음식을 선택하고 주문할 때
example_1: I’d like to order this, please.
example_2: Can I order this? I’d like to order this.

expression: Can I get the bill, please?
situation: 식사를 마치고 계산할 때
example_1: Can I get the bill, please?
example_2: We’re ready to pay. Can I get the bill, please?

expression: I’d like a table for two.
situation: 레스토랑에서 자리 예약/요청을 할 때
nuance: 인원 수를 명확히 말하는 기본 주문 표현
example_1: Hi, I’d like a table for two, please.
example_2: Do you have a table for two tonight?

situation: 채식 여부를 확인할 때
example_1: Do you have vegetarian options?
example_2: I’m vegetarian. Do you have vegetarian options?

situation: 호텔에서 추가 수건을 요청할 때
example_1: Could I get extra towels, please?

example_2: Could you tell me what time boarding starts?

situation: 공항에서 게이트를 찾을 때

example_2: How long does it take to get there from the hotel?

expression: Could you call a taxi for me?

expression: Can I get an extra towel?

example_2: The Wi-Fi isn’t working today. What can I do?

example_1: Do I need to make a deposit for the reservation?
example_2: Is there a deposit required when booking a table?

situation: 도시/관광지/역 위치를 찾아갈 때

example_2: How much is a ticket to the city center?

expression: Could you help me check in?
situation: 공항에서 셀프 체크인이 어렵거나 직원에게 체크인 도움을 요청할 때

example_2: Excuse me, could you help me check in at this kiosk?

situation: 공항 도착 후 짐을 찾으러 갈 때

expression: Could I get an extra towel?

expression: Do you have any tables available tonight?

example_2: If you have any openings, we’d love to come in tonight.

expression: I have a food allergy—what do you recommend?
translation_ko: 저는 음식 알레르기가 있어요. 무엇을 추천해 주실 수 있나요?
situation: 알레르기/금기 식품이 있을 때 안전하게 주문하려고 할 때
example_1: I have a food allergy—what do you recommend that’s safe for me?
example_2: I’m allergic to peanuts. Could you recommend something without them?

expression: Is the tap water safe to drink?
situation: 물 안전 여부를 확인할 때(해외 여행 시 자주 사용)
example_1: Is the tap water safe to drink here?
example_2: Before I order, is the tap water safe to drink?

expression: Could we get the bill, please?
situation: 식사를 마치고 결제할 때
example_1: We’re ready to pay—could we get the bill, please?
example_2: Could we get the bill, please? Thank you.

expression: Where should I line up for security?
translation_ko: 보안 검색은 어디에서 줄 서면 되나요?
situation: 공항에서 검색 대기줄 위치를 찾을 때
example_1: Where should I line up for security? I don’t see the sign.
example_2: Excuse me—where should I line up for security?

expression: How do I get to the city center from here?
situation: 도착 후 교통편/경로를 물을 때
nuance: 가장 흔한 길찾기 질문(부담 없는 톤)
example_1: How do I get to the city center from here?
example_2: What’s the best way to get to the city center from the airport?

situation: 명소/역/식당까지 도보 가능 여부를 확인할 때
example_1: Is the museum within walking distance?
example_2: Is the train station within walking distance from here?

expression: I’m trying to get to the nearest ATM.
translation_ko: 가장 가까운 ATM이 어디인지 찾고 있어요.
situation: 현금이 필요해서 ATM 위치를 찾을 때
example_1: I’m trying to get to the nearest ATM—could you point me in the right direction?
example_2: Where can I find the nearest ATM? I’m trying to withdraw cash.

expression: Could you recommend a reliable taxi service?
translation_ko: 믿을 만한 택시 서비스를 추천해 주실 수 있나요?
situation: 이동 수단을 안전하게 선택하려 할 때
example_1: Could you recommend a reliable taxi service from the hotel?
example_2: I’d appreciate your recommendation for a trustworthy taxi service.

expression: Would it be easier to take the subway instead?
situation: 대안 교통수단을 비교할 때
example_1: Would it be easier to take the subway instead of a bus?
example_2: I’m not sure about the route—would it be easier to take the subway?

expression: Could you help me with the check-in process?
situation: 공항에서 셀프 체크인 기계나 카운터 절차가 복잡할 때
example_1: Excuse me, could you help me with the check-in process for my flight?
example_2: I’m not sure how to check in online—could you help me with the check-in process?

expression: Where is the baggage drop-off counter?
translation_ko: 수하물 위탁(짐 맡김) 카운터가 어디에 있나요?
situation: 공항에서 짐을 맡겨야 할 때
example_1: Where is the baggage drop-off counter for international flights?
example_2: Could you tell me where the baggage drop-off counter is, please?

expression: I’d like to confirm my boarding time, if possible.
situation: 탑승 시간이 애매하거나 안내 방송을 놓쳤을 때
example_1: I’d like to confirm my boarding time, if possible, because I’m running a little late.
example_2: Could I confirm my boarding time at the gate, please?

expression: What gate is my flight leaving from?
situation: 출발 게이트를 확인해야 할 때
nuance: 급하지 않되 핵심 정보를 빠르게 묻는 톤
example_1: Can you tell me what gate my flight is leaving from?
example_2: I can’t find the signs—what gate is my flight leaving from?

expression: Is there a lounge I can use with this ticket?
translation_ko: 이 티켓으로 이용할 수 있는 라운지가 있나요?
situation: 공항 라운스 이용 가능 여부를 물을 때
example_1: Is there a lounge I can use with this ticket, or do I need a membership?
example_2: I’d like to rest—could you tell me if there’s a lounge available?

expression: Could you tell me where the nearest ATM is?
translation_ko: 가장 가까운 ATM이 어디 있는지 알려주실 수 있나요?
situation: 현금이 필요해 공항/도시에서 위치를 찾을 때
example_1: Could you tell me where the nearest ATM is in this terminal?
example_2: I need some local currency—could you tell me where the nearest ATM is?

expression: I have a reservation under the name of ____ .
situation: 호텔/식당/서비스에서 예약 확인이 필요할 때
nuance: 정확한 신상 정보 확인을 위한 포멀한 톤
example_1: Hello, I have a reservation under the name of Kim Min-ji.
example_2: I have a reservation under the name of Park Jiyoon for two nights.

situation: 체크인 가능 시간(얼리 체크인/지연 체크인 포함)을 확인할 때
example_1: What’s the check-in time, exactly? I don’t want to miss it.
example_2: Do you have an early check-in option, and what’s the check-in time?

expression: Do you offer early check-in or late check-out?
situation: 이른 도착/늦은 출발로 시간 조정이 필요할 때
example_1: Do you offer early check-in or late check-out for guests?
example_2: We arrive early—do you offer early check-in or late check-out?

expression: Could I request a room on a higher floor?
translation_ko: 높은 층의 객실로 배정받을 수 있을까요?
situation: 전망/조용함을 위해 객실 위치를 요청할 때
nuance: 부탁이지만 부담 없이 원하는 선호를 전달하는 톤
example_1: Could I request a room on a higher floor, if available?
example_2: I’d like a quieter room—could I request a room on a higher floor?

expression: Is breakfast included in the room rate?
situation: 숙박 요금에 포함 여부를 확인할 때
nuance: 비용 관련 조건을 확인하는 실속 있는 톤
example_1: Is breakfast included in the room rate, or is it an additional charge?
example_2: I’m comparing options—could you confirm whether breakfast is included?

expression: What time does breakfast start and end?
translation_ko: 조식은 몇 시에 시작해서 몇 시까지인가요?
situation: 조식 운영 시간을 확인할 때
example_1: What time does breakfast start and end on weekdays?
example_2: Could you let me know what time breakfast starts and ends?

expression: I’d like to place a request for extra towels.
situation: 객실 내 필요한 물품이 모자랄 때
example_1: I’d like to place a request for extra towels, please.
example_2: Could I request extra towels for two guests?

expression: Is there Wi‑Fi available, and is it included?
translation_ko: Wi‑Fi가 제공되나요? 그리고 요금에 포함되어 있나요?
situation: 객실 인터넷 사용 가능 여부와 요금 조건을 확인할 때
example_1: Is there Wi‑Fi available, and is it included in the price?
example_2: Do you have Wi‑Fi available in the rooms, and is it included?

expression: Could we get a table by the window, if possible?
translation_ko: 가능하다면 창가 자리로 부탁드릴 수 있을까요?
situation: 식당에서 자리 배정을 요청할 때
example_1: Good evening—could we get a table by the window, if possible?
example_2: Could we get a table by the window, please? It would make our evening more enjoyable.

expression: Are there any specials on the menu tonight?
situation: 주문 전에 오늘의 특선/추천을 물을 때
example_1: Are there any specials on the menu tonight that you’d recommend?
example_2: What are the specials on the menu tonight, if any?

expression: I have an allergy to ____ . Could you advise me?
translation_ko: 저는 ____ 알레르기가 있어요. 무엇을 먹어야 할지 조언해 주실 수 있나요?
situation: 알레르기/식이 제한을 안전하게 알릴 때
example_1: I have an allergy to peanuts. Could you advise me on what I can safely order?
example_2: I have a gluten intolerance—could you advise me, please?

expression: Could I get the bill, please?
situation: 식사를 마치고 계산할 때
example_1: We’re ready to leave—could I get the bill, please?

expression: Do you take credit cards, or is cash preferred?
translation_ko: 신용카드는 되나요, 아니면 현금이 더 좋나요?
situation: 결제 수단을 확인할 때
example_1: Do you take credit cards, or is cash preferred here?
example_2: Before we order, I’d like to know whether you take credit cards.

expression: What do you recommend for a first-time visitor?
situation: 현지 맛집/대표 메뉴를 추천받고 싶을 때
nuance: 상대의 경험을 존중하는 친근하고 공손한 톤
example_1: What do you recommend for a first-time visitor—something that’s truly local?
example_2: I’m here for the first time. What do you recommend?

expression: How long does it take to get there by public transit?
situation: 이동 시간/교통편을 계산할 때

example_2: Could you tell me how long it takes to get there by public transit?

expression: Could you show me on the map, please?
situation: 정확한 위치/경로를 이해하기 어려울 때
nuance: 상대에게 시각적 도움을 요청하는 친절한 톤
example_1: I’m not from around here—could you show me on the map, please?
example_2: Could you show me on the map where I should get off the subway?

situation: 길을 찾는 중에 즉시 방향을 물어볼 때

example_2: Can you tell me which way I should go from here to reach the station?

translation_ko: 환승 없이 바로 가나요, 아니면 갈아타야 하나요?
situation: 지하철/버스/대중교통 이용 시 노선 정보를 확인할 때
example_1: Is there a direct route to downtown, or do I need to transfer?
example_2: To get to the airport, is there a direct route, or do I need to transfer?

expression: I’d like to book a taxi for a specific time.
situation: 호텔/프런트에서 픽업 시간 예약이 필요할 때
nuance: 시간 약속을 명확히 하는 정중한 톤
example_1: I’d like to book a taxi for a specific time this afternoon, please.
example_2: Could you help me book a taxi for 7:30 a.m. tomorrow?

situation: 상대가 요즘 뭘 하는지 물을 때

example_2: What are you up to right now?

situation: 오랜만에 보거나 처음/재만남 인사할 때
example_1: Nice to see you again!
example_2: Nice to see you. How have you been?

example_2: Don’t worry. That’s okay.

situation: 상대가 실망/미안해할 때 괜찮다고 해줄 때

example_2: Don’t worry. It’s okay.

example_2: Do you want to come with me?

example_2: Let’s try that restaurant—Sounds good!

example_2: That’s not a good idea. I don’t think so.

example_2: Sorry, I don’t remember your name. What’s your name?

situation: 자기소개를 할 때
example_1: Hi, my name is Mina.
example_2: Nice to meet you. My name is Daniel.

situation: 가까운 사이에서 나이를 물을 때(상황에 따라 조심)

example_2: I’m twenty. How old are you?

nuance: 간단한 칭찬으로 분위기를 좋게 하는 말

example_2: I like your hair today. It looks great.

situation: 같이 뭔가 하자고 제안할 때
example_1: Do you want to grab coffee after school?
example_2: Do you want to watch a movie tonight?

situation: 즉흥적으로 함께 하자는 제안/제의할 때
example_1: Let’s go for a walk.
example_2: Let’s meet at the park at 5.

situation: 상대의 제안을 듣고 바로 동의할 때
example_1: —Let’s eat now. Sounds good to me.
example_2: We could try that new restaurant. Sounds good to me.

situation: 상대의 계획/제안이 즐거워 보일 때
example_1: Trip to the beach? That sounds fun!
example_2: Going out for dinner tonight? That sounds fun.

situation: 함께 하겠다는 의사를 간단히 말할 때
example_1: You’re going to the game? I’m in!

example_1: There’s a party on Saturday—count me in!
example_2: I’d love to join. Count me in.

situation: 가까운 시일 내에 다시 만날 예정일 때
example_1: I’ll text you. See you soon!
example_2: Take care. See you soon.

situation: 약속 장소/시간에 늦었을 때
example_1: Sorry, I’m late. Traffic was bad.
example_2: Sorry, I’m late. I’ll be there in five minutes.

situation: 상대가 안부를 물어본 뒤 고마움을 표현할 때
example_1: Thanks for asking. I’m doing well.
example_2: How are you? Thanks for asking!

situation: 짧게 이야기할 시간이 필요할 때
example_1: Do you have a minute? I need to ask you something.
example_2: Sure. What’s up?

situation: 상대가 추후 상황을 알려주길 바랄 때
example_1: If you change your plan, let me know.
example_2: Okay, I will. I’ll let you know tomorrow.

situation: 약속 장소에 참석하겠다고 확인할 때
example_1: Don’t worry. I’ll be there at 6.
example_2: See you soon—I’ll be there.

situation: 일정/약속을 다른 날로 제안할 때
example_1: We can’t do today. How about tomorrow?
example_2: I’m free tomorrow. How about tomorrow?

example_1: It’s been a while. We should hang out.
example_2: Are you free this week? We should hang out.

situation: 결정을 아직 못 했거나 정보가 부족할 때
example_1: I’m not sure. Let me check.
example_2: I’m not sure about tonight. What time?

situation: 지금 당장 정하기 어렵고 미루고 싶을 때
example_1: We can’t decide now. Let’s decide later.
example_2: No problem. Let’s decide later today.

situation: 장난으로 한 말이 오해를 살 때 정정할 때
example_1: You’re the boss, right? I’m just kidding.
example_2: Sorry, I said that seriously—I'm just kidding.

situation: 갑자기 다른 주제로 넘어가며 덧붙일 때
example_1: By the way, do you want to come with us?
example_2: I forgot to tell you. By the way, the movie starts at 7.

situation: 상대가 나가거나 뭔가 하러 갈 때 기분 좋게 응원할 때
example_1: We’re heading out now. Enjoy!
example_2: Have fun at the party—enjoy!

expression: What have you been up to?

example_1: What have you been up to lately?
example_2: Not much—just work and hanging out with friends. What about you?

situation: 누군가를 오랜만에 보거나 인사할 때
example_1: Good to see you again!
example_2: Good to see you too. How’s your week going?

situation: 구체적 날짜 없이 약속 잡을 때
example_1: I’d love to—let’s hang out sometime next week.
example_2: Sure! Let’s hang out sometime soon.

situation: 주말 약속을 잡을 때
nuance: 직접적이지만 자연스러운 질문. 계획을 세울 때 자주 사용.
example_1: Are you free this weekend? We could grab dinner.
example_2: I might be—what did you have in mind?

expression: Do you want to grab coffee?
situation: 가볍게 만나기(커피/음료/간식)를 제안할 때
nuance: 부담 없는 제안. 친한 친구 사이에서 특히 흔함.
example_1: Do you want to grab coffee after work?
example_2: That sounds great—let’s do it.

expression: I was just thinking about you.

example_1: I was just thinking about you. How have you been?
example_2: That’s so sweet. I’ve been okay—what about you?

situation: 모임/행사 진행 상황을 확인할 때
nuance: 간단하고 실용적인 질문. 대화의 흐름을 이어가기에 좋음.
example_1: What’s the plan for tonight?
example_2: We’ll meet at six and then go to the movies.

situation: 좋았던 만남/행사를 끝내고 다음을 제안할 때
nuance: 친근하고 긍정적인 분위기. 관계를 더 이어가고 싶은 톤.
example_1: That was fun—we should do this again.
example_2: Definitely. We should do this again soon.

situation: 상대의 일정이나 방식에 맞춰줄 때
example_1: Can we move it to tomorrow? That works for me.
example_2: Sure—3 pm works for me.

situation: 제안에 캐주얼하게 동의할 때
nuance: 매우 캐주얼한 톤. 친한 친구 사이에 적합.
example_1: Dinner at that place? I’m down for that.
example_2: Sure, I’m down for a walk if you are.

situation: 자세한 정보가 필요할 때(가능 여부/시간 등)
example_1: Can you make it tomorrow? Let me check.
example_2: Give me a minute—let me check my schedule.

situation: 추후 일정이나 변동 사항을 공유해달라고 할 때
example_1: If anything changes, just let me know.
example_2: Okay. I’ll let you know by tonight.

situation: 문제가 생겼을 때 대처할 때
nuance: 걱정은 줄이고 함께 해결하자는 긍정적인 분위기.
example_1: The plan changed last minute, but we can figure it out.
example_2: Don’t stress—we’ll figure it out together.

situation: 상대가 제안했을 때 바로 호응할 때
example_1: Let’s go to the new café downtown. That’s a great idea!
example_2: We could study at the library tomorrow. That’s a great idea.

expression: I’ll see what I can do.
situation: 확답은 어렵지만 시도해보겠다고 말할 때
nuance: 정중하고 현실적인 톤. 아직 확실하지 않을 때 자연스러움.
example_1: Can you help me move this weekend? I’ll see what I can do.
example_2: I can try. I’ll see what I can do.

situation: 약속을 취소/불참해야 할 때
example_1: Sorry, I can’t make it tonight.
example_2: I really wanted to come, but I can’t make it this time.

situation: 사소한 부탁/실수에 대해 상대가 사과할 때
nuance: 강하게 괜찮다는 뜻. 상대를 안심시키는 톤.
example_1: Sorry about that.
example_2: No problem at all. It happens.

situation: 상대 의견에 동의할 때
nuance: 짧고 자연스러운 동의. 논쟁 없이 합의할 때 자주 사용.
example_1: We should leave now. You’re right.
example_2: I think so too—you’re right.

situation: 대화를 하다가 떠오른 내용을 꺼낼 때
example_1: That reminds me—I need to call my mom.
example_2: That reminds me, have you bought the tickets yet?

situation: 중요하거나 흥미로운 이야기를 시작할 때
nuance: 상대의 주의를 끌고 비밀/이야기 톤을 만드는 표현.
example_1: Let me tell you something. I found an awesome place to eat.
example_2: Let me tell you something—I’m really excited about it.

situation: 대화 중 잠깐 물어볼 게 있을 때
nuance: 예의 있게 주제를 꺼내는 톤. 짧게 끝낼 것 같은 분위기.
example_1: I have a quick question. What time are we meeting?
example_2: I have a quick question—can you help me with this?

situation: 무례하지 않게 허락을 구할 때(가벼운 요청)
nuance: 상대 배려가 느껴지는 정중한 질문. 일상에서도 자주 사용.
example_1: Do you mind if I sit here?
example_2: Do you mind if I take a quick call?

situation: 바쁘지만 만나자는 제안일 때
nuance: 부담 없는 약속 제안; 정확한 날짜를 정하지 않아도 되는 편안한 분위기
example_1: We should catch up sometime this week.
example_2: Sure—let’s catch up sometime next month.

expression: Do you have any plans tonight?
situation: 친구에게 그날 저녁 계획을 물을 때
nuance: 자연스럽게 약속을 제안하기 위한 질문; 공손하지만 가벼운 톤
example_1: Do you have any plans tonight?
example_2: Not really—why? Do you want to grab dinner?

situation: 가볍게 만날 때, 캐주얼 약속 제안할 때
nuance: 친근하고 즉흥적인 느낌; 부담을 줄인 제안
example_1: Want to grab a coffee after work?
example_2: That sounds great—let’s go.

situation: 만날 시간을 조율할 때
nuance: 구체적인 가능 시간 제시; 실용적이고 명확한 톤
example_1: I’m free after 6 if you want to meet.
example_2: Okay, I can meet you after 6.

situation: 제안을 받아들일 때
example_1: Movie night? I’m up for it.
example_2: Are you free to study together? I’m up for it.

translation_ko: 별거 아니야 / 크게 신경 쓰지 마
situation: 사소한 문제를 가볍게 넘길 때
nuance: 부정적인 감정을 최소화; 상황을 축소하는 완화 톤
example_1: You forgot the tickets? It’s not a big deal.
example_2: Don’t stress—it's not a big deal.

situation: 안부 묻거나 연락한 사람에게 감사할 때
nuance: 예의 있고 따뜻한 감사 표현; 진지한 배려가 느껴짐
example_1: Thanks for checking in—I really appreciate it.
example_2: I didn’t expect you to call, but thanks for checking in.

situation: 도움이나 배려를 받았을 때
nuance: 감사를 강하게 표현; 정중하면서도 진심이 담김
example_1: I really appreciate you helping me out.
example_2: Thanks— I really appreciate it.

expression: Do you want to split the bill?
situation: 식사/카페 비용을 나눌지 물을 때
nuance: 실용적이고 부담 없는 제안; 친근하지만 상황을 명확히 함
example_1: We can split the bill, right? Do you want to split the bill?
example_2: Sure. Do you want to split the bill or pay separately?

situation: 일이나 활동을 마감할 때
nuance: 캐주얼한 마무리; 더 이상 이어서 하지 않겠다는 자연스러운 종료 표현
example_1: I’m getting tired. Let’s call it a day.
example_2: We’ve done enough for today—let’s call it a day.

expression: We should do this again sometime
situation: 좋았던 만남을 마무리하며 다시 약속 제안할 때
nuance: 따뜻하고 긍정적인 마무리; 장기적인 관계를 암시
example_1: This was awesome. We should do this again sometime.
example_2: Next time, let’s try a different place. We should do this again sometime.

situation: 상대의 비용/대접을 내가 부담하겠다고 할 때
nuance: 관대하고 배려 있는 톤; 상대에게 부담을 덜어줌
example_1: You paid last time—this time, that’s on me.
example_2: Don’t worry about it. That’s on me.

situation: 제안에 즉흥적으로 동의할 때(가벼운 친구 사이)
nuance: 매우 캐주얼하고 긍정적인 톤; 친한 사이에서 자연스러움
example_1: Dinner at 8? I’m down.
example_2: Wanna go out tonight? I’m down.

situation: 상대가 수상해 보이거나 상황을 잘 모르겠을 때
nuance: 직설적일 수 있어 주의; 장난스러운 톤이면 자연스럽지만 때로는 따질 듯 들릴 수 있음
example_1: You seem stressed—what’s the deal?
example_2: I don’t get it. What’s the deal with this plan?

situation: 헤어질 때 다음 만남을 암시할 때
example_1: Okay, I have to go now. I’ll see you soon.
example_2: Thanks for hanging out. I’ll see you soon.

situation: 만나서 근황을 물을 때
nuance: 일상적인 안부 질문, 부담 없는 톤
example_1: Hi! How have you been since we last talked?
example_2: How have you been? You seem busier than usual.

expression: What have you been up to lately?
situation: 최근 근황을 더 구체적으로 궁금해할 때
example_1: What have you been up to lately? I’ve missed hearing from you.
example_2: What have you been up to lately—work or something new?

situation: 누군가 컨디션이 좋아 보이거나 멋있게 꾸몄을 때
nuance: 격려와 칭찬의 톤, 가볍고 부담 없게
example_1: You look great—did you get a haircut?
example_2: You look great today. What’s the occasion?

translation_ko: 거기 완전 대박이겠다/엄청 멋질 것 같아.
situation: 상대가 한 계획이나 경험을 듣고 크게 공감할 때
nuance: 흥분과 긍정이 섞인 반응, 리액션이 적극적
example_1: We’re going to try that new ramen place tonight—sounds amazing!
example_2: You’re training for a marathon? That sounds amazing.

situation: 함께하자고 제안받았을 때 바로 수락할 때
example_1: Let’s grab dinner after work—I'm totally in.
example_2: If you’re going to that concert, I’m totally in.

situation: 가벼운 제안을 할 때(식사/산책/카페 등)
example_1: Do you feel like grabbing coffee later?
example_2: Do you feel like going for a walk after dinner?

expression: I’d love to, but I can’t.
translation_ko: 하고 싶긴 한데, 그건 못 해.
situation: 정중하게 거절할 때
nuance: 거절하지만 예의를 갖춘 톤, 관계를 해치지 않음
example_1: I’d love to, but I can’t make it tonight.
example_2: I’d love to join, but I can’t because I’m tied up.

situation: 당장은 어렵지만 추후 가능성을 남길 때
nuance: 상대에게 부담을 덜 주는 완곡한 표현
example_1: I can’t do it this weekend—maybe another time.
example_2: I’m swamped today, but maybe another time works for me.

translation_ko: 정말 배려해 줬네/너무 신경 써 줘서 고마워.
situation: 선물, 도움, 배려를 받았을 때
example_1: You got me that book—That’s so thoughtful.
example_2: Thanks for offering to help. That’s so thoughtful of you.

situation: 사과를 받았거나 실수가 있을 때 바로 안심시킬 때
example_1: Sorry I’m late—No worries at all.
example_2: I forgot to tell you, but no worries at all.

translation_ko: 생각이 너무 복잡하게 가지 말자/과하게 생각하지 말자.
situation: 걱정이 커진 상황에서 가볍게 넘기자고 할 때
example_1: We don’t have to worry that much—let’s not overthink it.
example_2: It’ll be fine. Let’s not overthink it.

situation: 상대의 감정이나 의견을 인정할 때
nuance: 공감 표현이지만 즉시 해결책을 제시하진 않는 반응
example_1: I hear you. It’s frustrating when things change last minute.
example_2: I hear you, but we should still look at the facts.

situation: 상대에게 맡겨진 일을 이어받아 주도할 때
nuance: 책임을 지는 리더십 톤, 신뢰를 주는 표현
example_1: Thanks for the details. I’ll take it from here.
example_2: Don’t worry—I’ll take it from here and update you later.

situation: 자주 못 본 친구와 재회 계획을 잡을 때
nuance: 진심 어린 약속 제안, 부담 없는 미래 제안
example_1: We should get together soon. Coffee next week?
example_2: It’s been a while—we should get together soon.

expression: Let me know what you decide.
situation: 선택을 기다리며 상대에게 연락을 요청할 때
example_1: I’m flexible—let me know what you decide.
example_2: Take your time. Let me know what you decide.

situation: 도움이나 배려에 진심으로 감사할 때
nuance: 정서적으로 깊은 감사 표현, 따뜻한 관계감
example_1: Thanks for covering for me— I appreciate you.
example_2: I appreciate you checking in. It meant a lot.

situation: 상대의 주장이나 의견에 동의하며 한 발 더 보탤 때
nuance: 생각을 존중하는 공감, 논의가 자연스럽게 이어짐
example_1: You’re right about the timing—that’s a good point.
example_2: That’s a good point. We should consider the cost too.

situation: 상대의 말이 공감하거나 필요한 순간에 나와줄 때
example_1: I’m glad you said that. I was thinking the same thing.
example_2: I’m glad you said that—I didn’t want to be the only one concerned.

translation_ko: 해결 방법은 찾을 수 있어/나중에 풀리겠지.
situation: 불안하거나 난처한 상황에서 확신을 주고 싶을 때
example_1: The details are a bit messy right now, but we’ll figure it out.
example_2: Don’t stress—we’ll figure it out together.

expression: By the way, did you hear about…?
situation: 친구에게 가볍게 관심을 보이며 새로운 이야기를 꺼낼 때
example_1: By the way, did you hear about the new café opening downtown?
example_2: By the way, did you hear about the concert everyone’s talking about?

translation_ko: 말도 안 되게도(설마) 그럴 확률이 있네?
situation: 우연히 뜻밖의 일이 맞아떨어졌을 때
example_1: We ran into the same person at two different places—what are the chances?
example_2: You ordered the same drink as me; what are the chances?

expression: I’m not going to lie, that surprised me.
situation: 감정을 솔직하고 자연스럽게 표현할 때
example_1: I’m not going to lie, that surprised me.
example_2: I’m not going to lie, the way it ended caught me off guard.

situation: 상대의 제안에 긍정하며 반응할 때
example_1: We should walk there instead—actually, that’s a good idea.
example_2: Let’s meet earlier tomorrow. That’s actually a good idea.

situation: 부드럽게 부탁하거나 제안을 할 때(상대에게 부담 주지 않으려는 상황)
nuance: 배려가 있는 톤, 거절 여지를 남김
example_1: No pressure, but could you send me that link when you get a chance?
example_2: No pressure, but would you want to grab a quick bite later?

expression: We should totally do this again.
situation: 함께한 시간이 좋았을 때 재약속을 제안할 때
nuance: 열정적이고 긍정적인 공감, 친한 친구 사이에 잘 어울림
example_1: This was so much fun—we should totally do this again.
example_2: Next time, we’re doing this again. We should totally do this again.

situation: 식사나 커피 등 비용을 대신 내겠다고 할 때
example_1: Want another round? It’s on me.
example_2: I insisted on dinner once—so let me pay this time. It’s on me.

situation: 어려울 것 같던 일이 성공했을 때
example_1: I can’t believe it worked. That was the last thing I expected!
example_2: I can’t believe it worked out—thank you for helping me.

situation: 상대가 내가 하려던 말을 먼저 해주었을 때
example_1: You read my mind—I was about to ask the same thing.
example_2: You read my mind. I was just thinking we should take a break.

expression: That said, I’m still not sure.
situation: 긍정 후에 불확실성을 덧붙일 때
example_1: It sounds promising—that said, I’m still not sure.
example_2: I like the idea; that said, I’m still not sure it fits our schedule.

situation: 너무 격식 차리지 않게 하거나 분위기를 편안하게 만들고 싶을 때
nuance: 부담을 줄이고 분위기를 가볍게 만드는 톤
example_1: We don’t need to dress up—let’s keep it casual.
example_2: Let’s keep it casual today. No big plans, just good vibes.

situation: 지금 당장은 확답이 어렵지만 추후 확인해 다시 말할 때
nuance: 업무적 뉘앙스가 있지만 일상에서도 ‘추후 연락’ 의미로 자연스러움
example_1: I need to check my schedule, but I’ll circle back to you.
example_2: I’ll circle back to you once I hear back from them.

expression: Let me know what you think.
situation: 의견을 요청하며 부담 없이 피드백을 기다릴 때
example_1: Send me the draft when you can, and let me know what you think.
example_2: Try it and let me know what you think.

situation: 상대의 이야기를 듣고 집중하겠다고 할 때
example_1: I’m all ears—what happened?
example_2: I’m all ears. Tell me everything from the beginning.

situation: 상대의 말에 논리적/합리적이라고 인정할 때
example_1: I get why you’d be upset. That’s fair.
example_2: You have a point—yeah, that’s fair.

situation: 서로 이해와 의견이 맞았다고 할 때
example_1: Great—sounds like we’re on the same page.
example_2: Let’s do it that way. We’re on the same page.

situation: 상대가 걱정하거나 양해를 구할 때 적극적으로 안심시키는 말
example_1: Thanks for moving it. I don’t mind at all.
example_2: If you’re late, I don’t mind at all—just text me.

expression: Could you give me a hand?
situation: 가볍게 부탁할 때(짐 옮기기, 설명해주기 등)
example_1: Could you give me a hand with these bags?
example_2: Could you give me a hand fixing this? I’m stuck.

situation: 무언가를 추천하며 기대를 전할 때
example_1: Try this place—you’ll like it. I think you’ll like it.
example_2: Start with the appetizer first. I think you’ll like it.

situation: 오랜만에 만나거나 연락했을 때 자연스럽게 꺼내는 말
example_1: Hey! It’s been way too long. How have you been?
example_2: It’s been way too long since we hung out like this.

situation: 상대가 더 좋은 경험을 했거나 좋은 소식을 들었을 때
example_1: You got tickets to that show? I’m jealous—in a good way.
example_2: That trip looked amazing. I’m jealous—in a good way.

situation: 믿기 어려운 소식이나 예상 밖의 상황에 반응할 때
nuance: 놀람과 약간의 불신, 친한 사이에서 장난스럽게 가능
example_1: You finished the whole report in one night? You’ve got to be kidding!
example_2: You’re moving to Seoul next month? You’ve got to be kidding.

situation: 상대의 긍정적인 태도에 격려하며 추켜세울 때
example_1: We might be late, but we’ll make it. That’s the spirit!
example_2: Keep going—you’re doing great. That’s the spirit.

situation: 처음 만나거나 가볍게 안부를 물을 때
nuance: 가장 기본적인 인사+안부 질문이라 친근하고 편안한 톤
example_1: Hi, how are you?
example_2: Hi, how are you today?

situation: 안부를 물었을 때 상태가 아주 나쁘지 않을 때
nuance: 무난하게 괜찮다는 뉘앙스, 너무 자세히 말하긴 싫을 때도 사용
example_1: How are you? Not too bad.
example_2: I’m feeling okay— not too bad.

situation: 컨디션이나 기분을 좋다고 말할 때
example_1: I’m feeling good today. How about you?
example_2: Thanks! I’m feeling good today.

situation: 피곤하다고 가볍게 말할 때
nuance: 강하지 않게(조금) 말해서 부담 없이 전달
example_1: Sorry, I’m a little tired.
example_2: I’m a little tired today, but I’m okay.

situation: 먹고 싶다고 바로 말할 때
nuance: 즉각적이고 단순한 표현이라 자연스러운 일상 톤
example_1: I’m hungry. Let’s eat soon.
example_2: I’m hungry—what should we get?

expression: What do you want to eat?
situation: 함께 식사 메뉴를 정할 때
nuance: 상대 의견을 물으며 진행하는 자연스러운 대화 톤
example_1: What do you want to eat tonight?
example_2: Let’s decide. What do you want to eat?

situation: 식당에서 메뉴를 주문할 때
example_1: Hi, I’ll have the chicken sandwich.
example_2: Can I get the menu? I’ll have the chicken sandwich.

situation: 여럿이 먹고 각자 돈을 내고 싶을 때
example_1: Can we split the bill, please?
example_2: Let’s split the bill. Is that okay?

situation: 음료를 마시고 싶을 때
example_1: I’m thirsty. Can I get some water?
example_2: I’m thirsty—do you want anything to drink?

expression: I need to see a doctor.
situation: 몸이 많이 아프거나 진료가 필요하다고 말할 때
example_1: I need to see a doctor. I feel really bad.
example_2: My stomach hurts a lot. I need to see a doctor.

expression: Do you have any pain medicine?
situation: 약국/편의점/약을 파는 곳에서 도움을 요청할 때
nuance: 구체적인 요청이라 상황에 딱 맞는 톤
example_1: Do you have any pain medicine?
example_2: Excuse me, do you have any pain medicine for a headache?

situation: 증상을 간단히 말할 때

example_2: I’m not sure— is it going to be hot today?

example_2: I like this weather a lot.

example_1: How much does it cost?
example_2: How much does it cost for this one?

situation: 큰 돈을 내거나 잔돈이 필요할 때
nuance: 급하게 필요할 수 있으니 친절하고 간단히

example_2: Do you have change? I only have a 20-dollar bill.

example_2: Sorry, I can’t— I have an appointment at 3.

situation: 도움이 필요할 때 정중하게 요청

situation: 요청을 받았을 때 바로 도와주겠다고 할 때

example_2: Sure, I can help you with that.

situation: 어디를 찾아야 하는지 안내/질문할 때

example_2: Excuse me, I’m looking for the pharmacy. Where is it?

situation: 실수/불편을 일으켰을 때 가볍게 사과할 때

example_2: I’m sorry about that. Are you okay?

situation: 결과/물건/상황이 기대와 다를 때 불만을 완곡하게 말할 때

example_2: That’s not what I expected. The taste is different.

situation: 음식 취향을 말할 때
example_1: I don’t like spicy food. Do you have something mild?
example_2: I don’t like spicy food, so I’ll skip this.

expression: I usually play games at home.
situation: 일상 습관/취미를 말할 때

example_1: What kind of music do you like?
example_2: I’m curious—what kind of music do you like?

situation: 연락을 다음에 해달라고 요청할 때

example_2: Can you text me later, please?

expression: Please call me when you’re free.
situation: 상대가 여유 있을 때 연락해달라고 부탁할 때

example_2: Please call me when you’re free. It’s important.

situation: 컨디션이 안 좋을 때 가볍게 말할 때

example_2: Sorry, I’m feeling tired after work.

example_2: That’s great news! I’m in a good mood now.

nuance: 일상적인 표현으로, 진료를 요구하는 느낌은 아님.

example_2: Sorry, I can’t stay long. I’m not feeling well.

situation: 몸의 증상을 말할 때
example_1: I have a headache. Do you have any medicine?
example_2: I’m sorry I’m late— I have a headache.

situation: 식당에서 주문할 타이밍일 때
nuance: 캐주얼하지만 식당 상황에 맞는 실용 표현.
example_1: The menu looks great. Can we order now?
example_2: Excuse me, can we order now, please?

situation: 새 음식이나 메뉴를 권했을 때

example_2: It looks good. I’ll try it, thanks.

situation: 디저트를 먹지 않겠다고 말할 때
example_1: I’m going to skip dessert today.
example_2: I’m full, so I’m going to skip dessert.

nuance: 필요할 때 바로 쓸 수 있는 기본 표현.
example_1: Excuse me, where’s the bathroom?
example_2: Where’s the bathroom, please? I really need to go.

example_2: If it doesn’t improve tomorrow, I’m going to see a doctor.

situation: 음식/약 관련해서 알레르기를 확인할 때

example_2: I’m allergic to peanuts—do you have any peanut-free options?

situation: 날씨 변화를 알아챌 때

example_2: It’s starting to rain, so bring your umbrella.

nuance: 강하지 않은 묘사로 일상 대화에 적합.

example_2: Yeah, it’s pretty hot today. I’m sweating.

example_2: I heard it might snow— is it going to snow later?

example_2: It’s getting dark. We should go home soon.

example_2: Sure—go ahead and try it on.

expression: I think it’s a little expensive.
situation: 가격이 부담스럽다고 말할 때
nuance: 직설적이지만 불친절하지 않게 비용 부담을 표현.
example_1: I think it’s a little expensive. Do you have a cheaper one?
example_2: The price is okay, but I think it’s a little expensive for me.

situation: 시간이 없어서 자리를 떠야 할 때
nuance: 부담 없이 일정 때문에 나가야 함을 알리는 톤.

example_2: I have to leave soon. Can we talk again later?

example_2: Traffic is bad. Is it okay if I’m late by 20 minutes?

situation: 도착 확인용으로 요청할 때

example_2: Sure. I’ll text you when I get there.
